output:
# Data catalogue (CRM sandbox)

This file is what the agents read to know which data exists.
In a real CRM team this is the "CRM data catalogue". The better the descriptions here, the better the SQL the agent writes.

Engine: **SQLite**. Dates are text `YYYY-MM-DD`. Use `date('2026-10-19')` as "today" (the data is synthetic and frozen on that date).

## customers (1 row per customer)
| column | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| customer_id | int | key |
| first_name | text | first name, used for personalisation |
| signup_date | text | sign-up date |
| country | text | PT, DE, ES, FR, UK |
| preferred_lang | text | pt, de, es, fr, en |
| age_band | text | 18-24, 25-34, 35-49, 50-64, 65+ |
| loyalty_tier | text | none, gold, platinum |
| has_app | int | 1 = has the app installed and logged in |
| email_consent | int | 1 = accepted marketing email. **Required for email.** |
| push_consent | int | 1 = accepted push. **Required for push.** |

## rentals (1 row per rental)
| column | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| rental_id | int | key |
| customer_id | int | FK to customers |
| pickup_date / return_date | text | start and end of the rental |
| branch_city | text | city of the pickup branch |
| branch_type | text | airport, city |
| vehicle_class | text | economy, compact, suv, premium, van |
| booking_channel | text | web, app, partner |
| revenue_eur | real | rental revenue |

Notes:
- "First-rental customer" = exactly 1 row in `rentals`.
- A customer can have 0 rentals (signed up and never rented).

## app_events
| column | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| customer_id | int | FK |
| event_date | text | event date |
| event_type | text | install, login, search, booking_start |

## rental_ratings (post-rental rating, last 60 days)
| column | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| rental_id | int | FK to rentals |
| customer_id | int | FK to customers |
| rated_at | text | rating date |
| score | int | 1 to 5. Low rating = score <= 2 |
| topic | text | car_condition, waiting_time, price, staff, pickup_process |

## crm_sends (communication history)
| column | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| campaign_id | text | campaign |
| customer_id | int | recipient |
| variant | text | A, B, C... or HOLDOUT (control group that received nothing) |
| channel | text | email, push |
| sent_at | text | send date |
| opened / clicked / converted | int | 0/1. converted = booking within the next 14 days |

## Business rules (applied by the code, not by the agent)
- No consent, no send. The pipeline automatically removes anyone without `email_consent = 1`.
- Fatigue: anyone who received a communication in the last 7 days is removed.
- A segment must return **one `customer_id` column, with no duplicates**.
- Minimum size for A/B: 600 customers after exclusions.

content.text: First rental = exactly 1 row in rentals. I will count these customers by how long ago they returned the car and by whether they have the app, to see how big each slice is.

input.sql:
SELECT CASE WHEN d <= 90 THEN '030-090' WHEN d <= 180 THEN '091-180' ELSE '181+' END AS bucket,
       c.has_app,
       COUNT(*) AS n
FROM (
    SELECT customer_id,
           julianday(date('2026-10-19')) - julianday(MAX(return_date)) AS d
    FROM rentals
    GROUP BY customer_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) = 1
) f
JOIN customers c USING (customer_id)
WHERE d >= 30
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2

SELECT CASE WHEN d <= 90 THEN '030-090' WHEN d <= 180 THEN '091-180' ELSE '181+' END AS bucket,
       c.has_app,
       COUNT(*) AS n
FROM (
    SELECT customer_id,
           julianday(date('2026-10-19')) - julianday(MAX(return_date)) AS d
    FROM rentals
    GROUP BY customer_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) = 1
) f
JOIN customers c USING (customer_id)
WHERE d >= 30
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2

content.text: The objective says 1 to 3 months and app adoption. First attempt: only people without the app, returned 30-90 days ago. That is 518 before exclusions; it may come up short, but it is the closest match to the request.

input.name: first_rental_30_90d_no_app
input.sql:
SELECT r.customer_id
FROM rentals r
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id
WHERE c.has_app = 0
  AND r.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM rentals GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) = 1)
  AND julianday(date('2026-10-19')) - julianday(r.return_date) BETWEEN 30 AND 90
input.rationale: Customers with a single rental, returned 30-90 days ago, without the app. This is the slice closest to the request.

output.error: After exclusions 340 customers remain; the minimum is 600. Widen the criteria.

content.text: Rejected: after consent and fatigue 340 remain, below the minimum of 600 for an A/B test. I have two levers: widen the window or include people with the app. Including app users even helps the test (I can compare), and widening to 180 days keeps customers still 'warm'. I will do both and leave has_app as a dimension for the content, not as a filter.

SELECT r.customer_id
FROM rentals r
WHERE r.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM rentals GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) = 1)
  AND julianday(date('2026-10-19')) - julianday(r.return_date) BETWEEN 30 AND 180

content.text: Profile: ~1.2k customers, 60% without the app, 60% picked up at an airport, mostly economy/compact, booked mostly on the web. Hypotheses: (A) a simple reminder as baseline; (B) personalising with the last city adds relevance; (C) an app-only incentive converts and pushes adoption. First draft of C:

content.text: The linter caught three problems: subject too long, 20% above the 15% maximum, and the term 'free'. I change it to 10%, drop the upgrade and shorten it. Submitting the three variants.

title: 7. Evaluation (code, statistics)
detail:
# Results

| group | n | open % | click % | conversion % | lift vs holdout | p-value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HOLDOUT | 122 | - | - | 4.92 | - | - |
| A | 369 | 31.4 | 7.3 | 4.61 | -6% | 0.888 |
| B | 369 | 33.9 | 5.7 | 5.42 | +10% | 0.830 |
| C | 369 | 32.0 | 5.1 | 4.61 | -6% | 0.888 |

**Best variant:** B (p-value vs holdout = 0.830).

**Statistical power:** to detect a 30% relative lift on a base rate of 4.9% you would need ~3843 customers per group. This test has ~369 per group.

Conclusion: **inconclusive**. Do not declare a winner. Options: accumulate more sends (continuous test), fewer variants, or a goal with a higher base rate (e.g. clicks).

*These results come from a simulated send (src/pipeline.py -> _true_uplift).*
